english.title: Violence on board ship likely to endanger the safe navigation of it
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), unlawfully and intentionally committed on board a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS..), an act of violence constituting an offence

(A)_[of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..),]_
(B)_[under section **(..SPECIFY SECTION..), of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861,]_
(C)_[under section 2 of the Explosive Substances Act 1883,]_

which was likely to endanger the safe navigation of the said ship
english.legislation: Contrary to section 11(1)(c) and (6) of the Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required.
(ii) See section 11(7) for offences that constitute 'an act of violence'.
(iii) See section 17 for definitions.
(iv) See also offence wording: H4299.
(v) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
